newsitem.title: USA: ComEd Zion 1 Ill. nuke seen shut for 3 wks.
newsitem.headline: ComEd Zion 1 Ill. nuke seen shut for 3 wks.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co's 1,040 megawatt (MW) Zion nuclear power unit 1 was expected to be out of service for three weeks following a shutdown for repairs, a company spokesman said Monday.
The unit was shut late Friday for repairs to a diesel generator, and would be "down about three weeks," said spokesman Gary Wald.
In addition to repairs to the generator, ComEd will also complete surveillance testing that was originally scheduled for a planned outage in May, Wald said.
"It will not now be coming down in May," the spokesman said.
Zion 1 had been operating at near 40 percent of capacity prior to the weekend outage, and would return to the 40 percent level following the shutdown, Wald said.
The unit is expected to operate at the 40 percent level through the summer, although it will be capable of ramping up to a full load if an increase in power demand makes it necessary, he said.
Zion 1 is scheduled for refueling and maintenance in the fall of 1997.
The Zion nuclear power unit 2, also at Zion, Ill., is expected to return to full service in March after a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage which began September 18.
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
